questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The main aspects have been the opportunity to choose courses in English at the university and the student life. The host city itself was also important to me, I wanted to choose a place that I wanted to explore. The handbook received in the beginning was also a good place to look for information before arriving.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: LUISS was quite good at communicating the important information to us and they were helpful and quick to answer. The website is also helpful and has the necessary description of the courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We didn't receive much information about exams, midt-terms and assignments in the beginning of the courses which caused some confusion.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were 4 people looking for an apartment together and it was a little bit hard to find something suitable. It seemed that it was easier to find separate rooms than whole apartments. We looked on different websites and Facebook, but it is important to be careful as some of the posts and messages are scams.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Rome is quite well connected with the metro so it is a good idea to find accommodation close to a station so it is easier to get around. The metro is also more reliable than the busses and tramp. 

During my exchange, 50% of all lectures were online so it was fine to live a bit further from the campus as I didn't have to be there every day, however it might be a good idea to prioritize living close to the uni if all lectures are on campus. The area close to uni is nice and a lot of Erasmus students live there, so it is easier to connect and find someone living close by.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing available through Luiss was quite expensive and therefore not very attractive. Most of the people find their housing on their own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration was fine. The description of courses was available on the website and the ''drop out'' period of time in the beginning of the semester is also good to choose the right courses and avoid time overlap.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to choose courses and register for them on the Web Self Service. You have to find the courses on the website or a list provided by Luiss. It is the student's responsibility to check if there are any time overlaps between courses. As we have to choose 5 different courses, it was a bit hard to find courses that don't overlap but it is also possible to choose courses from other faculties, which helps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Mobility office at Luiss was helpful and answered e-mails quickly. LUISS also provided the students with courses available. The website and time table website is also very useful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the descriptions carefully and check courses from other faculties as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is generally lower than at the University of Copenhagen. The courses are all only 6 ECTS, but the curriculum is quite large and does not correspond with the ECTS-points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is mostly a traditional lecture - the teacher is presenting a Powerpoint and the students are listening. The involvement of students vary from course to course, but it is possible to engage with the professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Regulatory Innovation, Legal issues in Marketing, Diplomacy and Negotiation, EU law before Courts and EU Private Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Legal Issues in Marketing. The professor is very well-structured and good at explaining lectures in a clear and understandable
manner.The
course is interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are some expenses related to the student association ESN (ERASMUS STUDENT NETWORK) that organizes the Welcome Week and other activities during the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: local transportation was less expensive than excepted (35 EURO a month).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The were some opportunities for exchange students, but I did not attend any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some sport teams and the ESN group, that organized activities for the exchange students. The ESN group also organized a football tournament for the exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to attend the Welcome Week and the trips organized during the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city of Civita di Bagnoregio was very beautiful and intersting - it is possible to combine it with Orvieto or other towns in Umbria. I would also recommend visiting Castel Gandolfo - 45 minutes from Rome by train. It is best to visit is early on, when the weather is still nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and very interesting to experience

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are always some Italian students attending the courses, so it is possible to connect to them there. There is also a student association that organizes parties for both Italian and exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit frustrating to adjust to the less structured way of teaching.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, history and energy/laid back style of the Italian people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) if you have any problems reach out to the Mobility Office, 2) there are a lot of materials uploaded on the courses sites but it is not necessary to read/study everything, 3) pay attention to the Powerpoints - those are the exam materials.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to study at an Italian university and test my academic abilities in new environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to studying in English and having 5 different courses at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
